Movers in Houston charge $250–$375 an hour for the crew of 5 that a house of 4 or more bedrooms usually needs, and the move costs $1,800–$4,300 in total at 10 road miles, off peak, with no stairs or extras. A 1-bedroom apartment runs $380–$960 on the same terms. That's how much do movers cost Houston households before minimums, travel, heat and the drive across town add their share.

How much do movers cost Houston households, by home size

Houston movers bill a local move by the hour. Each mover is billed at $50–$75 an hour on a typical local move with a truck, so a crew's rate rises with every mover. That's why how much do movers cost Houston households depends first on the size of the home, which sets the size of the crew:

  • a studio or 1-bedroom apartment gets 2 movers, at $100–$150 an hour;
  • a 2-bedroom home gets 3 movers, at $150–$225 an hour;
  • a 3-bedroom house gets 4 movers, at $200–$300 an hour;
  • a house of 4 or more bedrooms gets 5 movers, at $250–$375 an hour.

In total, a studio move costs $280–$740, a 2-bedroom home $720–$1,800 and a 3-bedroom house $1,150–$2,850, each at 10 road miles, off peak, with no stairs and nothing extra. They come from the rate table behind the calculator, not from Houston quotes, so treat them as a check on the estimates you collect.

A 4-bedroom house in Katy, priced step by step

Say you're moving a 4-bedroom, two-story house from one Katy subdivision to another, about 10 road miles apart. The baseline is a crew of 5 at $250–$375 an hour, and $1,800–$4,300 for the job. Then the details of a real Houston house come in, and each one adds to how much do movers cost Houston homeowners:

  • The stairs. In a two-story house, the furniture from every upstairs bedroom comes down a flight of stairs.
  • The garage. Tools, bikes, yard gear and a second refrigerator in the garage can add an hour or more.
  • Packing. A packing crew for a home this size adds $1,100–$2,800.
  • The date. The calculator prices a date from May through September as peak season, which is also the hottest stretch of the year.

Enter your own stairs, date and packing in the calculator above to see where your house lands, and how much do movers cost Houston homeowners once those details are counted.

Minimums, trip fees and 15-minute billing

Hourly quotes in Houston often carry terms that change the total more than the rate does. Some Houston movers publish rates with a 2-hour minimum, a trip fee on top of the hourly rate, billing in 15-minute steps, and a higher rate on Fridays and weekends than midweek. Others bill travel time by the hour instead of a trip fee. Before you compare how much do movers cost Houston renters at two companies, ask each one:

  • Is there a minimum number of hours, and does it include the drive?
  • Is there a trip fee, or is travel time billed by the hour?
  • Is time billed in full hours, half hours or 15-minute steps?
  • Does the rate change with the day of the week?
  • Are fuel, tolls, shrink wrap or mattress bags charged on top?

On a small job, those terms decide the bill. With a 2-hour minimum, a crew that finishes a studio in 90 minutes is still paid for 2 hours, plus any trip fee, so how much do movers cost Houston renters for a small move can sit well above the rate times the hours worked.

What the hourly rate pays for

The rate you pay for each mover isn't what that mover takes home. The pay panel below shows what hand laborers and material movers earn an hour in the Houston metro area, by Bureau of Labor Statistics figures. The gap between that and $50–$75 an hour covers the truck, fuel, insurance, equipment, licensing and the company's overhead. That's why how much do movers cost Houston customers can't be worked out from crew wages alone, and why a quote far below the going rate deserves a closer look.

Katy to The Woodlands: drive time across Houston

Houston covers a lot of ground, and plenty of moves run from inside the 610 Loop out to Katy, Cypress, Sugar Land, Pearland or The Woodlands. On an hourly move, the drive between addresses is crew time, so a trip across town on I-10 or I-45 at rush hour costs more than the same load moved a few miles. Toll roads such as the Sam Houston Tollway can shorten the drive, and some movers pass the tolls on. Ask how the drive is billed, and pick a start time that misses the worst traffic, so the route adds as little as it can to how much do movers cost Houston families.

Moving between Houston and Austin, San Antonio or Dallas? Those moves stay inside Texas, and the distance table below gives the road miles and a price range for each, the way the calculator counts them.

Heat, humidity and hurricane season

Summer is peak season in the calculator, and in Houston it's also hot and humid for months on end. Crews need water and breaks, and work slows in the afternoon, so an early start helps. Humidity is hard on wood furniture, electronics and anything left in a truck or an unconditioned storage unit, so ask for padding and wrapping, and keep the time your things spend in transit short.

The Atlantic hurricane season runs from June 1 to November 30, and a tropical storm or a heavy downpour can flood streets and postpone a move at short notice. If you move in those months, ask about the mover's rescheduling policy before you sign, keep a second date in mind, and pack important papers and medicine to travel with you. A storm delay can add days to a truck rental or a lease overlap, and that is part of how much do movers cost Houston households in a bad week.

Texas paperwork for a Houston move

Movers that work inside Texas must be licensed with the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV), as the licensing panel below shows. Two Texas rules also shape the paperwork you get:

  • Your rights sheet. Under 43 Tex. Admin. Code §218.55, a mover that gives you a written proposal must also give you the TxDMV's information sheet, Your Rights and Responsibilities When You Move in Texas.
  • Cargo liability. Under §218.53, Texas adopts the federal rule, 49 CFR 375.201, as its voluntary standard for a mover's liability for your goods. FMCSA explains the levels of liability that rule sets.

Read the sheet before moving day, and ask which level of liability the price includes, because extra cover adds to how much do movers cost Houston households. The TxDMV's consumer page, Don't Make a Move Without Us, also has a section on a mover's liability against transit insurance, and a link to look up a mover's certificate number.

Driving it yourself with hired loaders

If the quotes run high, doing the driving yourself is the main alternative, and it's the surest way to cut how much do movers cost Houston renters. You rent the truck, and a labor-only crew of 2 loads or unloads it for $80–$130 an hour, or $40–$65 an hour for each mover. The truck guide below shows which size your rooms need, and the comparison after it prices the same move with a rental truck, a container and a full crew. Remember the costs a quote from movers already covers: fuel, a dolly and pads, and your own time.

How much do movers cost Houston families who leave Texas?

Once a move crosses the state line, federal rules apply, and the price follows weight and miles, not hours. A house of 4 or more bedrooms moved 1,000 road miles costs $5,700–$11,800, off peak and with no stairs or extras, or about $5.71–$11.72 per mile spread over the distance. An interstate mover must be registered with the FMCSA, hold a USDOT number and give you a written estimate. FMCSA's Protect Your Move sets out your rights on a move between states.

A written answer to how much do movers cost Houston homeowners

  1. Enter both ZIP codes, your home size, date and stairs in the calculator above. It's free, takes about a minute and needs no email to see your price.
  2. Check each mover's TxDMV certificate number for a move inside Texas, or its USDOT number for a move out of the state.
  3. Ask for a written proposal after the mover has seen your things, along with the rights sheet.
  4. Ask about minimums, trip fees, billing steps and day-of-week rates, and get the answers in writing.

Set the proposals side by side with the calculator's range, and ask about any line that falls outside it. That's how you learn how much do movers cost Houston homeowners like you before anyone carries a box.

Key takeaways

The main numbers on this page, in a few lines.

  • A 2-bedroom home move takes up about 640–930 cu ft: the smallest truck that holds the heavy end is 20 ft.
  • By law, Texas movers must be licensed with the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles, and a licensed mover has an active TxDMV certificate number.

  • Tip guides suggest $4–$15 per mover per hour: $16–$98 per mover for 4–6.5 hours on site, $48–$294 for 3 movers.
  • Harris County had 114 moving companies with paid employees in 2023: 2.4 per 100,000 residents, against 2.8 across the US.
  • The moving checklist has 14 tasks, from 8 weeks before the move to moving day.
  • Most hand laborers and material movers in the Houston-Pasadena-The Woodlands, TX metro area earned $16 to $22 an hour in May 2025, against $17 to $23 across the US.
  • In Houston, 1 in 6 people moved in the last year, against 1 in 8 across the US.
  • A 2-bedroom home move of 10 road miles, off peak: $58–$103 with a rental truck before help, $390–$1,380 with a container, and $720–$1,800 with full-service movers.
  • Houston movers bill by the hour, and on a small move the minimum, trip fee and billing steps can matter as much as the rate.
  • A mover inside Texas must give you the TxDMV's rights sheet with its written proposal; a move out of state falls under federal rules.
  • From June to November, hurricane season can postpone a Houston move, so ask about rescheduling before you sign.

Tipping a crew after a humid Houston move

Tips aren't part of how much do movers cost Houston customers on the bill, but most guides suggest one. Work out a tip per mover by the hour or by the day, and for the whole crew.

3 movers 4–6.5 hours

Per mover $16–$98

For the crew $48–$294

Who to tip and when

  • Tipping is up to you: guides call a tip a thank-you for good work, not an obligation. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, This Old House and U-Haul)
  • Guides find cash simplest, handed to each mover at the end of the job. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, This Old House, MoveAdvisor and CNET)
  • When one crew loads and another unloads, guides suggest tipping each crew after it finishes its part. (HireAHelper, CNET, Real Simple, American Van Lines and NerdWallet)
  • On a move of several days, guides suggest tipping at the end of each day, in case the crew changes. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet and Forbes Home)
  • Guides suggest a separate tip for a separate packing crew. (CNET and This Old House)
  • Guides suggest asking the moving company about its tipping policy first: some build gratuity into the price, and some don't accept tips. (Forbes Home, This Old House and U-Haul)
  • Guides suggest tipping more for stairs, heavy furniture or bad weather, and less, or nothing, for damage, a late start or careless work. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, CNET and Real Simple)
  • Drinks and snacks are welcome, but guides don't count them as the tip. (NerdWallet and CNET)

What to do before a Houston moving day

Getting ready early keeps how much do movers cost Houston families close to the quote. Enter your date to see each task when it falls due, from three estimates and photos of valuables to the final bill.

0 of 14 done

8 weeks before

  • Paper or digital, keep every page a company gives you until the move is settled.

  • Give each one the same details, so the prices compare like for like.

6 weeks before

  • Get every possible extra charge listed on the estimate, so the price you pay is the price you were given.

4 weeks before

  • Label each box with its room and what's inside.

  • Get close-ups of any damage that's already there, so a claim later is clear.

  • Once your request is approved, USPS says to allow at least 7-10 business days for it to take effect. Standard forwarding lasts 12 months.

    Source: U.S. Postal Service

  • Have the old place stop the day after you leave, and the new place start the day before you arrive.

  • If another company will do the job, get its name and check it too.

2 weeks before

  • A sketch with each room named lets the crew put things in place on the first trip.

1 week before

  • Keys, gate or door codes, and someone there to let them in.

  • Chargers, basic tools, toilet paper, cleaning supplies, snacks and a change of clothes.

The day before

  • A change of clothes, toiletries and any medicine for the first night.

Moving day

  • Ask about any charge you don't recognize.

  • Point out anything fragile, very heavy or going to a particular room.

Questions

How much do movers cost Houston households? FAQ

Can't find your answer? Email hello@liftmyboxes.com.

How much do movers cost Houston renters for a small apartment?

A studio move costs $280–$740 and a 1-bedroom move $380–$960, at 10 road miles, off peak, with no stairs or extras, with 2 movers at $100–$150 an hour. On a job this small, a minimum number of hours or a trip fee can matter as much as the rate, so how much do movers cost Houston renters depends on those terms too.

Is a flat-rate quote cheaper than hourly movers in Houston?

Not always. A flat rate, set after the mover sees your things, shields you from traffic and a slow day, while an hourly rate can come out lower for a small move you've packed and staged well. Compare both on the same inventory, because how much do movers cost Houston households under either one depends on what's listed.

Should you rent a truck and hire loaders in Houston?

It can save money if you're happy to drive. A labor-only crew of 2 costs $80–$130 an hour to load or unload a truck you rent, so you pay for the truck, fuel and your own time instead of a full crew. It works best for a short move, and it lowers how much do movers cost Houston renters most when the crew only needs a couple of hours.

How much should you tip movers after a hot Houston move?

Tipping is up to you. Guides suggest a tip per mover by the hour or for the day, or a share of the bill, and many suggest a bit more for heat, stairs or heavy pieces. The tip calculator on this page works those published ranges out for your crew and hours.

How do you check a Houston mover before you book?

Look up its certificate number in the TxDMV's Truck Stop to make sure it is licensed, and read recent reviews for how it handled problems. Ask for a written proposal and the Texas rights sheet, and be wary of a price far below the others.
